notes: Research: Goldratt, The Goal (1984) and It's Not Luck (1994). TOC's five focusing steps (identify, exploit, subordinate, elevate, repeat) treat throughput as set by one constraint; the Evaporating Cloud (conflict resolution diagram) is one of the five Thinking Processes trees, laid out as A (objective) <- B, C (requirements) <- D, D' (prerequisites), with D and D' in conflict. The cloud's leverage is that the B-D and C-D' arrows rest on unstated assumptions; surfacing them and invalidating one (the injection) evaporates the conflict rather than compromising. Eight slots: goal/step/constraint carry the throughput view, objective/requirement/prerequisite/assumption/injection carry the cloud. Decision: assumption nodes are always derived (never stated by speakers), injection carries the idea field. | Scout returned three candidates: (1) CoreWeave/Brian Venturo 2025-07-15, (2) Groq/Jonathan Ross 2025-07-08 (HBM as the bottleneck), (3) AI capex wall 2025-10-23 (fabs vs energy). Chose (1): it is the only one where the SAME speaker names the binding constraint, eliminates the popular candidates with evidence, and then states the chronic conflict that constraint produces - so the cloud is about the constraint, which is the case the Evaporating Cloud exists for. (2) was strong but its injection is stated in the source (Groq removed the memory), which would leave the injection slot a fact and lose the framework's payoff; (3) is hosts reading an essay aloud, so the conflict is reported, not owned. | Decision: the constraint node c1 is a FACT here, against the registry's typical_provenance 'derived', because Venturo names it outright ('the biggest constraint is speculative capital'). The derived work moves to c2 (where the constraint goes next) and to the four assumptions. | Decision: four assumptions per example rather than five - the objective-to-requirement arrow on the survival side (a bankrupt company serves nobody) is trivially valid and adds a node without adding insight; it is noted in the README instead. | Decision: no idea field on the classic example, so the gold ring reads unambiguously as 'this is where the opportunity is' in the TBPN example only. | Only 3 of 29 TBPN edges are facts (el3, el4, ec2) against 7 of 20 in the classic. That is the example's real lesson, not a defect: written scenario prose states its own connectives ('to keep cost per part down he is expected to...'), diarised speech almost never does, so in a transcript the cloud's arrows are all inference. | Resume: the first framework-agent process was killed after the README child wrote README.md but before it was committed. The resuming agent verified the untracked README field by field against graph.json (every node and edge id cited, texts, labels, quotes, rationales, confidences and idea fields identical; all headings match the SPEC 6 template; all five relative links resolve) and kept it rather than relaunching a README child.
